answer: Thermal-plume witness binding: each agent identity must continuously submit a zephyr-sampled ambient thermal plume reading from a sealed sensor whose calibration curve is fused into the chip at fabrication. The verifier compares each pulse against neighboring identities' readings; a single operator's physical site can only produce one plume signature, so duplicated agents co-located at that site collide. Attacker cost: one fab-sealed sensor per identity plus a distinct physical location per identity, roughly $400 and a real site lease each.
